posts.title: Afternoon Sunwatch
posts.text:
☀️ Afternoon Sunwatch — September 13, 2026

🔆️ Solar activity: Low (B5.0)
🔥 Latest solar flare: B9.2 (Peaked September 13, 2026 at 18:01 UTC)
🔥 Strongest recent flare: B9.6 (Peaked September 12, 2026 at 23:23 UTC)
💨 Solar wind speed: 439 km/s (Moderate)
🌎 Geomagnetic activity: Quiet (Kp 1.00)

The Sun gave us a little flicker! 🔥

Large coronal-hole regions stand out in today’s solar images, while visible sunspots and active regions remain modest.

Image: NASA SDO/AIA — 131 Å
Data: NOAA Space Weather Prediction Center

posts.text:

posts.title: Coronagraph Watch
posts.text:
🔭 Coronagraph Watch — September 13, 2026

A new CME showed up in NASA’s DONKI, so Sunny is checking the Sun’s outer corona.

☀ CME start: September 13, 2026 at 01:24 UTC
💨 CME speed: 403 km/s
🏷 CME SCORE: S-type (<500 km/s)
📐 CME half-angle: 19° (Narrow)

Sunny is watching the corona. 👀🌌

Image: NOAA SWPC — CCOR-1
Data: NASA DONKI + NOAA Space Weather Prediction Center

posts.title: Midday Sunwatch
posts.text:
🌤️ Midday Sunwatch — September 13, 2026

🔆️ Solar activity: Low (B3.4)
🔥 Latest solar flare: B5.5 (Peaked September 13, 2026 at 10:48 UTC)
💨 Solar wind speed: 428 km/s (Moderate)
🌎 Geomagnetic activity: Quiet (Kp 1.33)

We're looking pretty quiet right now. 🤍✨

Large coronal-hole features stand out today, alongside modest active-region activity and only a few small sunspots.

Images: NOAA GOES-19 SUVI — 195, 284, 171, 304, 131, 094 Å
Data: NOAA Space Weather Prediction Center

posts.title: Early Morning Sunwatch
posts.text:
🌅 Early Morning Sunwatch — September 13, 2026

🔆️ Solar activity: Low (B3.8​)
🔥 Latest solar flare: B5.2 (Peaked September 13, 2026 at 06:07 UTC)
💨 Solar wind speed: 400 km/s (Moderate)
🌎 Geomagnetic activity: Quiet (Kp 2.00)

Quiet conditions out there. 🌎✨

Today's solar images show small sunspot groups, broad coronal-hole regions, and bright coronal loops, with no clear outward eruption visible.

Image: NASA SDO/AIA — 171 Å
Data: NOAA Space Weather Prediction Center
